text: Hello and welcome to live text commentary of the Premier League fixture between Sheffield United and Everton at Bramall Lane.
When these teams look back at results at the end of the season, this game could stand out with significant importance.
It’s early days, but both clubs could be in danger of relegation with Sheffield United recently returning to the top flight and Everton escaping the drop by the skin of their teeth last season.
There is a huge three points up for grabs today.
The big news in the Sheffield United camp is that Archer makes his Premier League debut for the club after completing a move from Aston Villa.
He starts alongside McBurnie up top, while Larouci replaces Ben Osborn at left-back.
There is also a Premier League bow for Everton striker Beto.
He scored on his debut against Doncaster Rovers during an impressive cameo off the bench in midweek, and is straight into the team for this game.
His inclusion is the only change from last week’s defeat to Wolves, replacing Lewis Dobbin.

Both Sheffield United and Everton have lost each of their first three league games this season; this will be only the fifth occasion of two sides facing each other on 0 points in a Premier League match having both played at least three games, after Southampton v Swindon in August 1993, Portsmouth v Bolton in September 2009, Sheff Utd v Fulham in October 2020, and Arsenal v Norwich in September 2021.
The teams have emerged from the tunnel and are ready for kick-off.
The match is underway at Bramall Lane.
Everton have an early free-kick out wide which is whipped in by Garner, but easily dealt with by the home side.
The visitors have started quickly.
Great defensive work from Onana, who makes a perfectly timed sliding challenge to dispossess Hamer as he looks to make a run into the box.
This is only the fourth game of the season for these teams, but there is a nervy atmosphere in Sheffield.
Both teams, already, cannot really afford to lose this one.
Everton are yet to score or pick up a point in the Premier League this season.
Only in 1926-27 (first five) and 1958-59 (first six) have the Toffees ever lost each of their opening four games of a league season in their history.

Meanwhile in English top-flight history, only four sides have ever lost and failed to score in their first four fixtures: Derby in 1899-1900, Stoke in 1906-07, Preston in 1924-25, and Crystal Palace in 2017-18.
Branthwaite is booked for a strong challenge on Hamer, who was making a dangerous run down the right wing.
United have a free-kick in a good position.
PICKFORD SAVES! Egan is unmarked at the back post and latches onto Norwood's free-kick with a header, but it's straight at the England international.
A warning for Everton.
United are slowly growing into the game.
They are trying to get Archer on the ball and inflict more threat on the Everton defence.
BETO STRIKES WIDE! The striker's shot from outside the box deflects wide and Everton have a corner.

GOAL! Everton finally have a Premier League goal and it comes courtesy of Doucoure from the corner! Foderingham does wonderfully to get down to his right and save a header that had deflected off Doucoure's knee, but the midfielder was in the right place to poke the rebound in.
Everton lead!
ANOTHER BIG CHANCE FOR EVERTON! Danjuma makes a direct run down the left flank and cuts inside on his right to get a shot away, which is deflected behind for another corner.
He had options and could have found a team-mate in a better position.
Pickford is called into action again to deny Larouci, who shoots low and hard, but it is easy enough for the England goalkeeper to stop.
GOOD SAVE FROM PICKFORD! He gets down low to turn away Hamer's effort and United have a corner.
Archer isn't having much luck at the moment.
He is trying to make things happen, but the defensive partnership of Branthwaite and Tarkowski have kept the 21-year-old quiet so far.
He could do with some more support at that end of the pitch.
Hamer keeps his composure to pass his way out of a tricky situation on the edge of the United box as Everton pressed.
It was risky, though.
McBurnie looks to play a through ball to Archer, but the pass is long and Branthwaite clears up again.
Frustration is growing at Bramall Lane.
CHANCE FOR EVERTON! Beto brings the ball down with his back to goal and looks to have lost possession as Robinson comes across to win the ball.
But the United defender passes it straight to Danjuma, who runs into the penalty box and shoots wide.
GOAL! ARCHER! United are level! Hamer works hard down the right to produce a cross and find McBurnie in the box.
He lays the ball off for Archer to slam home! A brilliantly worked goal.
It's brilliant from McBurnie, who keeps composed with his back to goal to find Archer.
That is the sort of support his strike partner has been crying out for, and he only needed one chance to make an impact.
How important could that goal be in United's season? Bramall Lane is rocking!

There have been just five goals scored in the five Premier League meetings between United (two) and Everton (three) at Bramall Lane before today, with no side scoring more than once in any of those games.
The game has gone up a level from the way it started.
It was edgy and cagey to begin with but those goals have opened it right up.
Vinicius is in the right place at the right time to head away a cross that Danjuma was waiting for unmarked at the back post.
There is a pause in the match as Egan requires treatment for a knock.
Egan is back on his feet and looks as if he is okay to continue.
United are momentarily down to 10 men as he waits for the signal from the referee.
DANJUMA WASTES A CHANCE! Beto plays a brilliant ball for Danjuma to run onto as he darts into the box.
But as he approaches the goal, his heavy touch lets him down as Foderingham comes off his line to recover possession.
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of the first half.
United are pushing for a second goal, they want to go into the break with the lead.
OWN-GOAL! 2-1 UNITED! Pickford won't want to see this again! Archer strikes against the woodwork with a fantastic effort and on the rebound, it hits Pickford on the back and goes in!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-1 EVERTON
What an ending to the half! United have turned around what was looking like a long day when Everton started brightly and took the lead through Doucoure.
But a moment of magic from Archer on his Premier League debut for the club got them back on level terms, before a stroke of luck put them in the lead.

England’s number one was unlucky to see the ball bounce off his back and into the roof of the net for United’s second, but the hosts had worked hard for a second goal before the break and got their reward.
Despite the fortunate goal for United, they have been more clinical offensively with the chances they have had.
Everton had a few good opportunities to extend their lead, twice through Danjuma, but have struggled to trouble Foderingham since their opener.
Beto looked sharp at points during the first half, but he needs to have more of an impact in the final third.
He may have squandered a couple of chances, but Danjuma is making things happen down the left and when Everton click, they could be in business.
This game isn't over!
The second half kicks off.
No changes for either side at the break.
There was concern surrounding Egan, who suffered a knock in the first half and took a while to shake it off.
But he is deemed fit enough to continue.
EVERTON WANT A PENALTY! Ahmedhodzic pulls down Beto right on the edge of the penalty box and Everton have a free-kick, but there is a check to see whether or not it was in the box.
The VAR check is complete and it will be a free-kick.
Ahmedhodzic is booked for the challenge.
It was really silly from the defender.
Danjuma takes the free-kick on the line of the penalty box, but he hits the ball straight into the wall.
It has been a lively start to the second half at Bramall Lane.
Young swings a corner in and Beto rises highest, but he heads the ball across the face of goal and wide.
GOAL! Danjuma equalises for Everton! They fly forward and Beto slips a ball to Patterson, who delivers a pinpoint cross towards the back post for Danjuma to finish excellently.
Patterson's cross put the ball on a plate for Danjuma.
It had just the right amount of pace on it to escape the United defence and find the winger, who made no mistake.
It is two goals in two games for Danjuma, who grabbed the winner in midweek against Doncaster.
Will it be the same again today?
United have a corner, but Pickford comfortably claims it.
There was not any attacking threat from the home side there.

Everton manager Dyche has won just one of his five meetings with United in all competitions (drawn two, lost two), losing both of his visits to Bramall Lane (3-0 in November 2019 and 1-0 in May 2021).
Baldock draws a foul from Doucoure as the pair jumped for a header.
It is becoming a real physical battle, as you would probably expect with these two teams.
Foderingham comes out to collect the ball, but the Everton fans behind his goal think he came out of his box.
The referee could not have been in a better position to make the call, and signals play on.
Larouci has gone down clutching his back and needs treatment.
Thomas is getting ready on the bench and will be coming on shortly.
Larouci will have to be replaced and Thomas comes on to make his debut after signing from Leicester City.
Egan is replaced by Basham in a double-change for United.
The home fans scream for a penalty as Baldock runs into Gueye, but nothing is given.
BRILLIANT SAVE FROM PICKFORD! Thomas is involved in the action straightaway and tests Pickford with a thumping effort at the back post, but the England goalkeeper makes himself big to keep it out.
There is a VAR check for an Everton handball in the penalty box, but it is completed quickly and no further action will be taken.
Doucoure concedes a foul, which he is cautioned for, and United have a free-kick in a good position just outside the box.
Hamer swings the ball in from the free-kick, but it is well-defended by Everton.
Everton make a change.
Garner comes off for McNeil.
There is a standing ovation for Archer, who is replaced by Traore.
Everton are winless in their last six Premier League away games against promoted sides (drawn three, lost three), having won five in a row before this streak.
Onana draws a foul from Basham just outside the box.
It is careless from Basham, who goes through the back of him, and now Everton have a brilliant chance to test Foderingham.
Young strikes at goal from the free-kick, but Foderingham saves comfortably.
Both teams are less than 10 minutes of normal time away from their first point of the season.
Of course, both sides want to win it, but they will be desperate not to lose from here.
United would escape the relegation zone if they can hold on for a point.
The game is finishing as it started, nervy.
Bramall Lane has gone quiet as Everton begin to control the latter stages.
It's really risky from Foderingham! But he keeps his composure as he brings down the ball with his feet, yards from goal, and lobs it over the onrushing Beto.
Doucoure looks for Danjuma in the box but Ahmedhodzic crucially cuts it out.
Tarkowski blocks a close-range shot from McBurnie with his head.
He needs to be seen to, but he is fine to play on.
However, as United have a throw-in, Tarkowski must exit the pitch for 30 seconds before he can come back on, and Dyche is fuming.
There will be six minutes of added time at the end of the second half.
There's plenty of time for a winner!
Tarkowski is replaced by Godfrey for the final stages.
Everton are controlling possession again as we edge towards full-time.
But every time United get near the ball, the crowd are urging them on.
The game is on a knife edge.
United have a free-kick and Hamer delivers the ball from deep, but Pickford rises highest to claim it.
We're past the allocated additional time, and United have a corner right at the death!
AN UNBELIEVABLE DOUBLE-SAVE FROM PICKFORD! McBurnie heads from the corner and Pickford pushes his effort onto the bar.
The ball falls back to McBurnie, who pokes towards goal, but Pickford is there to deny him again! What a finish to the game.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-2 EVERTON

That was a brilliant game of football! Despite both of these teams starting the game without a point, there were moments of real quality - and sheer luck! Everton took the lead through Doucoure before United pulled a goal back thanks to a brilliant finish from Archer.
The striker then rattled the woodwork before the ball unluckily ricocheted into the net off Pickford’s back.
But Everton found an equaliser through Danjuma, who was sharp throughout the game but lacked composure in front of goal until that moment.
Pickford then made a terrific double-save right at the death to stop McBurnie from snatching a winner.
Both teams, especially Everton, will be satisfied with a point.
Both teams are off the mark now and can certainly take a lot of positives from today's game.
There were bright league debuts for Archer and Beto who can make a big difference to their respective clubs this season.
After the international break, Everton host Arsenal at Goodison Park where they have a fairly good record against the Gunners, while Sheffield United travel to north London to face Tottenham Hotspur.
Thanks for joining us, goodbye!
